ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which greeting fits when you meet someone in the evening? (1 mark)
   A. sabaahu l-khayr
   B. ʿafwan
   C. maʿa s-salaama
   D. masaa'u l-khayr

2. Which Arabic sentence means "Who is this? (a boy or man)" (1 mark)
   A. مَنْ هَذَا؟
   B. هَذَا أَبِي
   C. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   D. هَذِهِ أُمِّي

3. Which Arabic sentence means "My sister reads." (1 mark)
   A. هَذِهِ أُمِّي
   B. أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ
   C. هَذَا أَبِي
   D. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ

4. What does the Arabic sentence الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The book is on the table.
   B. The lamp is above the table.
   C. The cat is under the bed.
   D. The pen is in the bag.

5. What does the Arabic word ayna ask? (1 mark)
   A. Who
   B. Where
   C. Why
   D. What

6. Which sound is in the name of the day al-khamiis? (1 mark)
   A. a heavy d
   B. a soft s only
   C. a hard k
   D. kh, a throat sound

7. What does the Arabic word الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) mean? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. day
   C. Sunday
   D. Tuesday

8. Which Arabic instruction means 'sit down'? (1 mark)
   A. qif
   B. ijlis
   C. ukhruj
   D. iqraʾ

9. Which word means 'with' in bi-yadii? (1 mark)
   A. ii
   B. fii
   C. bi
   D. yad

10. What does the Arabic sentence أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I write with my hand.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. I hear with my ear.
   D. I smell with my nose.

11. Which Arabic sentence means "This is my hand." (1 mark)
   A. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   B. هَذِهِ يَدِي
   C. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي
   D. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي

12. What happens to the voice at the end of a statement? (1 mark)
   A. It rises
   B. It falls
   C. It shouts
   D. It stops

13. What is the name of the Arabic letter خ? (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. thaa
   C. qaaf
   D. khaa

14. Which of these is true about the Arabic alphabet? (1 mark)
   A. It is read from left to right
   B. It has capital and small letters
   C. It has no capital letters
   D. It has only 20 letters

15. Which sound does the Arabic letter ك make? (1 mark)
   A. k as in kite
   B. n as in net
   C. j as in jug
   D. m as in mat

16. Which is the correct blend of the syllables a + bun? (1 mark)
   A. buna
   B. bana
   C. nuba
   D. abun

17. What does the Arabic sentence جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My brother is small.
   B. Hello, Ahmad.
   C. My grandfather is old (big in age).
   D. My sister is beautiful.

18. Which Arabic sentence means "On the table there is a cup." (1 mark)
   A. الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ
   B. أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ
   C. فِي الْمَطْبَخِ طَاوِلَةٌ وَكُرْسِيٌّ
   D. عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ

19. What does maadhaa mean? (1 mark)
   A. where
   B. who
   C. what
   D. why

20. Which Arabic word means "eggs"? (1 mark)
   A. بَيْضٌ
   B. ذُرَةٌ
   C. جَزَرٌ
   D. لَحْمٌ

21. Which Arabic word means "mouth"? (1 mark)
   A. جِسْمٌ
   B. فَمٌ
   C. رِجْلٌ
   D. يَدٌ

22. How is the Arabic word بَطْنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. jism
   B. raʾs
   C. batn
   D. rijl

23. What is the name of the Arabic letter ك? (1 mark)
   A. ʿayn
   B. shiin
   C. kaaf
   D. DHaa

24. What is the name of the Arabic letter م? (1 mark)
   A. baa
   B. jiim
   C. alif
   D. miim

25. What does the Arabic sentence الْكُرْسِيُّ جَدِيدٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The door is big.
   B. The window is clean.
   C. The chair is new.
   D. The table is small.

26. What does the Arabic word أُسْبُوعٌ (usbuuʿ) mean? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. yesterday
   C. Monday
   D. Wednesday

27. What does the Arabic sentence أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My mother cooks the food.
   B. We dance.
   C. I have a gift.
   D. I like the party.

28. Which Arabic word means "party"? (1 mark)
   A. شَمْعَةٌ
   B. حَفْلَةٌ
   C. تَفَضَّلْ
   D. أُغْنِيَةٌ

29. Which line of the poem means 'My nose smells'? (1 mark)
   A. famii yatakallamu
   B. ʿaynii taraa
   C. anfii yashummu
   D. udhunii tasmaʿu

30. Which sentence means 'The wind is strong'? (1 mark)
   A. al-jawwu mumtir
   B. al-jawwu ghaa'im
   C. ar-riihu qawiyya
   D. ash-shamsu haarra

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Translate into English: ashrabu l-maa'a (2 marks)

32. Read these words and write their sounds in English letters with meanings: مَرْحَبًا and شُكْرًا. (4 marks) (4 marks)

33. Translate into English: al-kursiyyu ʿinda l-baab (2 marks)

34. Read the sentence اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ and write its meaning. (2 marks) (2 marks)

35. Say where the pen is if it is in the bag. Write the sentence in English letters and translate it. (3 marks) (3 marks)

36. Write four Arabic celebration words in English letters with their meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

37. Explain how the voice should sound in a statement and in a question. (2 marks) (2 marks)

38. Translate into English: lii ʿaynaani (2 marks)

39. Write the Arabic sounds and meanings of four position words. (4 marks) (4 marks)

40. Translate: al-qittatu taHta s-sariir. al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila. (2 marks) (2 marks)

41. Describe how to carry out a dictation of the days of the week in pairs. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Write the seven days of the week in Arabic sounds, in order. (4 marks) (4 marks)

43. Explain why poems help us when learning a language. (2 marks) (2 marks)

44. Give two tips for pronouncing Arabic greetings correctly. (2 marks) (2 marks)

45. Translate into English: hal ʿindaka hafla? (2 marks)

46. Describe three steps of making a weather poster. (3 marks) (3 marks)

47. Translate into English: al-baabu kabiir (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: akhii Sagiir (2 marks)

49. Spell the word الخميس by naming its letters in order. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — masaa'u l-khayr
   masaa'u l-khayr means 'good evening'. sabaahu l-khayr is for the morning.

2. A — مَنْ هَذَا؟
   مَنْ هَذَا؟ (man haadhaa?) means: Who is this? (a boy or man)

3. B — أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ
   أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ (ukhtii taqraʾu) means: My sister reads.

4. B — The lamp is above the table.
   الْمِصْبَاحُ فَوْقَ الطَّاوِلَةِ (al-misbaahu fawqa t-taawila) means: The lamp is above the table.

5. B — Where
   ayna means 'where'.

6. D — kh, a throat sound
   The letter kh is a throat sound like a soft clearing of the throat.

7. C — Sunday
   الْأَحَدُ (al-ahad) means Sunday.

8. B — ijlis
   ijlis means sit down. qif means stand up.

9. C — bi
   bi means 'with', so bi-yadii is 'with my hand'.

10. A — I write with my hand.
   أَكْتُبُ بِيَدِي (aktubu bi-yadii) means: I write with my hand.

11. B — هَذِهِ يَدِي
   هَذِهِ يَدِي (haadhihi yadii) means: This is my hand.

12. B — It falls
   In a statement the voice falls at the end. In a question it rises.

13. D — khaa
   The letter خ is called khaa.

14. C — It has no capital letters
   Arabic has one style for each letter and no capitals.

15. A — k as in kite
   The letter ك makes the sound k as in kite.

16. D — abun
   The syllables are read in order: a then bun gives abun (father).

17. C — My grandfather is old (big in age).
   جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ (jaddii kabiir) means: My grandfather is old (big in age).

18. D — عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ
   عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ كُوبٌ (ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub) means: On the table there is a cup.

19. C — what
   maadhaa means what.

20. A — بَيْضٌ
   بَيْضٌ (bayd) means eggs.

21. B — فَمٌ
   فَمٌ (fam) means mouth.

22. C — batn
   بَطْنٌ is read batn and means stomach.

23. C — kaaf
   The letter ك is called kaaf.

24. D — miim
   The letter م is called miim.

25. C — The chair is new.
   الْكُرْسِيُّ جَدِيدٌ (al-kursiyyu jadiid) means: The chair is new.

26. A — week
   أُسْبُوعٌ (usbuuʿ) means week.

27. A — My mother cooks the food.
   أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ (ummii tatbukhu T-taʿaam) means: My mother cooks the food.

28. B — حَفْلَةٌ
   حَفْلَةٌ (hafla) means party.

29. C — anfii yashummu
   anf is nose and yashummu means smells.

30. C — ar-riihu qawiyya
   riih is wind and qawiyya is the feminine form of strong.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: I drink water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: mar-ha-ban (hello) and shuk-ran (thank you).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reading and 1 mark for each meaning.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The chair is at the door.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: ismii Ahmad. My name is Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reading and 1 mark for meaning.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: al-qalamu fii l-haqiiba. The pen is in the bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the item, 1 mark for the position word fii, 1 mark for the translation.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example ʿiid (festival), hafla (party), hadiyya (gift), kaʿka (cake).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: In a statement the voice falls at the end. In a question it rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have two eyes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: fii (in), ʿalaa (on), taHta (under), fawqa (above).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: The cat is under the bed. The lamp is above the table.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner says a day; the other repeats it, says the sounds and writes the letters from right to left; they check and correct together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the day, 1 mark for writing and 1 mark for checking.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: al-ahad, al-ithnayn, ath-thulaathaa', al-arbiʿaa', al-khamiis, al-jumuʿa, as-sabt.
   Working / marking points: 4 marks for all seven in order; 3 for five or six; 2 for three or four; 1 for one or two.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rhythm and rhyme help us to remember words and to practise pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for memory and 1 mark for pronunciation.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the teacher first and copy; say long vowels for longer than short vowels; practise the throat sounds kh and ʿ.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible tip.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw and colour the sun, clouds, rain and wind; write the Arabic word under each; add a sentence and a title and display it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: The door is big.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: My brother is small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: alif, laam, khaa, miim, yaa, siin.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six letters in order; 2 marks for four or five; 1 mark for two or three.
